script: Is Ødegaard lowkey having his best start to a season in an Arsenal shirt? Last season was the worst of Martin Ødegaard's Arsenal career. As the team's captain, he managed just one league goal and three assists the entire year. And along the way, he hurt his shoulder twice, wrecked his knee, and missed 24 matches through injury. But the way those injuries piled up dragged him into a record no Premier League player had ever set before him: Ødegaard became the first player ever to get subbed off in the first half of three games in a row, with shoulder trouble ending his day against Leeds and Nottingham Forest before his knee gave out against West Ham. Arsenal won the title that season, while their captain watched most of it from the sidelines. But the version of Ødegaard that showed up for the new season looked nothing like the one who limped through the last one. In the Community Shield against Manchester City, Ødegaard scored and got named man of the match in a 3-0 win, and then he scored again in the league opener against Coventry. Today against Chelsea, Arsenal fell behind after 77 seconds, and Ødegaard scored the winner five minutes into the second half, a goal that on its own doubled his entire league total from last season. He also created four chances and drew three fouls in a performance people are already calling a masterclass. So is this quietly his best start ever in an Arsenal shirt? His 22-23 season had 15 league goals, so the raw numbers say no. Yet after everything he went through, this is easily his most meaningful one.
